    Tuesday 20 October 2026

    Morning briefing · Evening court

    Morning briefing

    The share column ships flat at the room's median - 10 names, 0 of them short, their order an unshipped shadow (R81) - and the option column ships the room's own G_OPTION median on 10 legs (R79; the owner's ten a day - 0 DESK-FILLED, 3 R4-OVERFLOW (owner, 2026-10-06) at half stake), led by UNH 2026-10-30 $430C at 52.5; watchdog sits suspended on a congressional feed that still serves no record count, and the board sat after the open

    Executive summary

    EXPOSURE share -0.185 [n=10] / option +0.116 [n=10] - basis TO THE FREEZE (CHAIR-COMPUTED: Spearman of each shipped vector, the share one-medians and the option R79 medians, against each line's served pct_change_1d x sign(direction), the move from the prior close to the 11:19:51 ET freeze). Both are under 0.50, so no TAPE-CALL=CONTINUATION is owed and neither order is the morning's move restated. Mandate: Mix (any). REGIME. SPY 769.68 is +0.42% to the freeze but -1.07% over five sessions. VIX is 17.63: -4.39% today, +15.46% over five. The served regime stamp reads risk-off, and today's bounce is led by breadth (IWM +1.80%, QQQ +0.18%). The 10-year eased to 5.10 and the dollar to 101.67. The FFT composite projects +2.94% over ten sessions; I read it as one served input and give it no weight. No macro event date is served for today, and the only macro prints the desks quote are housing (pending home sales at a 25-year low). OVERNIGHT. Asia closed down: the Hang Seng -1.32% and Shanghai +0.12%; the Nikkei -0.62% and KOSPI +1.76% rows are STALE (last bar 2026-10-19). Europe is flat in session (FTSE -0.23%, DAX +0.18%, Euro Stoxx -0.06%). The futures pointed up into the open (ES +0.56%, NQ +0.43%). Asia and the futures disagree, which is the shape that most often retraces. Expected shape: a morning move that retraces and then reclaims - the open's lift fades into midday and climbs back through the 11:19:51 level by the close. The court can score it on SPY's close against 769.68. The board SAT AFTER THE OPEN, 109.9 minutes in (R158); R113's reason is not served to me, and the brief says FREEZE UNRECORDED. CONVICTION. The room's conviction sits in large-cap financials and defensives, not in the scanner's volume names: Spearman(score, volume_ratio) = 0.9066 says the slate is a volume sort. The share column makes three bets, not ten. (i) Financials: BAC 62, BLK 60, MS 60 - one bet on a financials bounce, best expressed by BAC. (ii) Fills of today's gap-down opens in industrials: GE 60, RTX 56, GM 55.5 - one bet, best expressed by GE. (iii) A with-tape tail: MCD 56, HLT 49, META 46, NOW 44.5. The option column is one bet: nine calls that large-cap quality rises into 2026-10-29. Its five defensive calls (UNH, WMT, CL, JNJ, ABBV) are one macro bet, best expressed by UNH (room 52.5, BE +3.28%, z 0.76 over 8.72 sessions). AAPL's 340P is the column's only offset.

    MODEL AND LEADER. The neural net disagrees sharply with the room on ACN (-9.05% over 5 days, against a call the room ranks third and the sheet's highest share median of 63). It also leans against JNJ (-3.28%), ABBV (-3.45%), V (-2.91%) and GM (-3.09%), and sides with the room's lukewarm reads on META (+4.99%) and RTX (+5.19%). The pyramid leader is the Black Swan (equity 111,551.76, rank 1), and its read carries no extra weight (R33). It diverges by grading payoff shape, not direction: it abstains on every share line I ship, and it grades CL's in-the-money 91C 30 against the room's 48.5 and COST's 910P 68 against the room's 9. Calibration: Graham's grade_return_corr of 0.087 is the highest served and the Oracle's 0.027 is next; every other is negative. None clears noise, and the 2026-09-27 backtest found no detectable edge, so I weight no seat up. R154(c) binds, because run 58's share reading was BELOW free, so no share rho is cited here as skill. The Decoder (SHADOW) abstains on all 20 lines I ship and enters nothing.     WHAT KILLS THE DAY'S TOP IDEAS: a close below 48.4 on BAC, below 286.07 on GE, or below 393.86 on UNH. A second kill among the five defensive calls on the same close ends that bet. The desk brief and my prompt agree on every figure I checked (36 of 40 contracts, the expiry counts, the freeze at 11:19:51 ET, leader blackswan). This is research, not advice. HOUSE RULES, decided before the session and not revisited inside it: (1) STAKES - share lines flat at 1.0 (R81). Option legs are 1.0 except JNJ and V at 0.5 under R4-OVERFLOW, and AMZN and CL at 0.5 so that whichever one the desk counts fifth on 2026-10-30 carries no override. That is 8.0 option units, 5.0 of them (62.5%) on 2026-10-30: a ONE-DATE BOOK of nine calls and one put. No adds on any line that is losing and no re-sizing. Second tickets on ACN, WMT, JNJ and AAPL, and a leg OPPOSITE an open claim on CIEN and AAPL, ship under the owner's fill (the room's top ten). They are recorded as stacked, not as hedges, and no further ticket opens on those names. (2) EXITS - each share line exits on its close-basis kill or at its stated horizon, whichever comes first. Each option leg follows its EXIT line: ratchet at its break-even, kill on the underlying's close, else close on the session before expiry (2026-10-29 for the 10-30 legs, 2026-10-22 for ABBV and CIEN, 2026-10-23 for AAPL).

    UNH, WMT, CL, JNJ and ABBV share one fate, so kills on two of them at the same close are read as the bet failing, not as two bad draws; the same holds for BAC, BLK and MS in the share column. (3) WINDFALL - when a leg's served mark reaches 2 x its premium at a freeze, half is banked at that mark and the record is written before the next freeze (R148); the other half rides to its own exit. Twelve open claims read WINDFALL STATE UNWRITTEN this morning, so no sentence of mine names an 'only unexecuted windfall', and tonight's R155(b) writer settles them before the next freeze. Desk, R92/R12 - the memo's listings against the persisted book: share: DIFF PRINTED (R92); option: DIFF PRINTED (R92)

    How this document was produced

    Live board session: FIFTEEN graders - the Decoder on its sheet number 17 - then the Skeptic and the Executive, each a separate model call over the same forty-candidate packet, answering the app's own prompts with each seat's most recent Evening Court lessons prepended. Collector data is real and timestamped. THE PACKET FROZE AT 11:19:51 ET, WITH 280 MINUTES OF TAPE LEFT BEFORE THE CLOSE: every entry is an early-afternoon mark, not an open, and under R14 a window that short makes seat ranks advisory.

    Lesson. I treat an out-of-the-money call as leverage on the sign over the court's one afternoon, not as a ticket to the tail: the 'times at three sigmas' multiple I print is a payoff at expiry that W cannot reach, so pricing a ticket as cheap against spot ranks the legs by how hard each one bets on direction. On 2026-10-20 each admitted call returned its underlying's move through its own realised leverage (dp_du_signed x briefing_price / premium_at_freeze: WMT 0.451 x 118.76 / 1.39 = 38.5, times -0.766 = -29.5; CIEN 0.662 x 344.64 / 9.70 = 23.5, times -0.781 = -18.4), my G_OPTIONs ran with that leverage (Spearman +0.800 [n=4], SEAT-COMPUTED; the code's WINGSORT -0.800 [n=4]), and on a day all four names fell my top two lost most; the premise that cheaper tickets pay read -0.685 [n=7] on run 58 and +0.800 [n=4] on run 59, so it has no sign of its own: its sign is whatever that day's underlying moves give it. This carries my 2026-10-12 lesson past the money, since over W even time value pays through delta. RULE: a premium's share of spot, a three-sigma multiple or the words 'cheap' or 'fair wing' move a G_OPTION only on a row that also prints DIR-CALL=<the sign I expect the name to take over this W, the served key path or dated event inside W that says so>; without that token the reading goes to key_risks and moves nothing, the row's stance names the sign its contract bets, and a row left with no other served reason files ABSTAIN (the owner's ruling (a)). CHECK, printed last with the self-check, labels and key paths only (R105): LEVER-ROWS=[every row a cheapness or three-sigma reading moved: ticker, its DIR-CALL key path or none], or none. TEST, registered now and computed by code by run id over the admitted legs wherever R29 admits a rho: LEVERSORT = Spearman(my G_OPTION, columns.option_column.legs.<t>.premium_at_freeze / day_report[ticker=<t>].briefing_price). It reads FAILED where LEVERSORT is negative (my grades again sorted on leverage), PASS where it is not, and UNDEFINED where R29 admits no rho; the premise Spearman(that ratio, contract_return_pct) prints beside it and is read, never fitted. Honest size: one court and four priced legs, under R29's floor, so the lesson is in-sample and SHADOW until that test passes; it promises no rho, and it stops me filing a bet on the sign under the name of convexity.

    Lesson. Room is evidence only where the crowd left it, not where the tape just made it. The distance from my price to the far line grows exactly as the price slides toward the near one. So before room lengthens a row's travel, I print the served five-day move, signed by the lead's direction, beside my two distances (slate_packet.json candidates[ticker=<t>].pct_change_5d); where my prompt does not serve it the row says '5D NOT SERVED - candidates[ticker=<t>].pct_change_5d' and room counts as my brief reads it. Where that move runs against the lead - a long that slid into its support, a short that rallied into its resistance - the near line is under test, not defended, and the room beyond it is the slide's residue. That row travels only on what stands at and behind the near line (a second level, a fib, a round number, or nothing), never on the room. Where the move runs with the lead, room counts as my brief reads it. The side still comes from the nearer line; this changes only how far a row travels. Evidence: ROOM, the order my grades follow, ran against the FIVE-DAY order on all five nights it has been read: -0.430, -0.285, -0.733, -0.673, -0.758 for runs 52, 54, 56, 58, 59 (court/common.json seat_orders_R154b_block.columns.share.orders.ROOM.by_run_id[*].vs_five_day.rho). It ordered the share lines +0.467, -0.503, +0.733, -0.285, -0.297 (.rho), a pooled +0.023 against +0.062 for the five-day order sign-flipped (columns.share_column.factor_panel_R128.by_run_id[*].FIVE-DAY.rho; the means SEAT-COMPUTED). My ROOM loading climbed +0.174, +0.772, +0.922 on runs 56, 58 and 59 while my FIVE-DAY loading fell +0.058, -0.322, -0.755 (seat_orders_R154b_block.columns.share.loadings_by_run_id[*].filed_seat_loadings.chartist.ROOM; five_day_loading_by_run_R154b.chartist.share), and tonight reads FACTOR=-FIVE-DAY. GM, graded 56 on a 'stacked floor' at 77.48 after a -6.26 five-day slide, broke it to 75.075 and closed -2.11 (day_report[ticker=GM]). It was chosen on the nights that show it, so it is in-sample: it rides SHADOW until its test passes, and it is NOT an edge I hold. This supersedes IN PART my 2026-10-14 lesson (member_journal[id=570]): 'the room the far line leaves' lengthens travel only where the five-day move did not make that room. TEST, registered tonight: from run 60, by run id over the next five courts sat (R56), the court reads ROOM's share rho (court/common.json seat_orders_R154b_block.columns.share.orders.ROOM.by_run_id[run_id=<r>].rho) beside -1 x the FIVE-DAY order's share rho (court/common.json columns.share_column.factor_panel_R128.by_run_id[run_id=<r>].FIVE-DAY.rho). It reads PASS if ROOM's pooled mean is at or below the sign-flipped five-day order's pooled mean over the same runs (room carried nothing the slide did not), and FAILED if above. A run where either is null reads UNDEFINED and does not count.

    Lesson. WHEN MY ROW NAMES AN OPEN CLAIM, MY NUMBER PRICES THE SECOND TICKET, NOT THE NAME. My key says a copy of a bet the book already carries adds cost and no edge, yet on run 59 I wrote it of WMT ('a second ticket on the same number is coverage, not edge') and of ACN ('a thin second ticket on the same bet') and still filed G_OPTION 60 and 56 where the room's medians read 49.5 and 50.0; both lost to time value alone (-29.50%, -21.43%) while the claim ACN copied (r66-run58-ACN, the $235C) banked its ratchet at the same close. So a same-sign OPEN-CLAIM print on the name is evidence against the new leg: I grade only what the new ticket adds beyond the claim already held - its own time value set against a move that claim already owns - and the row names the claim it read and which way it moved my G_OPTION, because words that call a leg coverage and a number that ranks it with my best cannot stand on one row. CHECK, each court, by run id: my G_OPTION on legs carrying a same-sign open claim (court/common.json columns.option_column.legs.<t>.open_claims_R114) beside my G_OPTION on the rest (court/croupier.json your_grades_vs_outcomes[instrument=option].your_grade), printed beside court/common.json diagnostics_R149b11.stacked_vs_unstacked.by_run_id[*].call - run 59: WMT and ACN 58 against CIEN and AMZN 54.

    Lesson. I clear my own sheet the way the court's reader does, operand by operand, not by the shape of the working: a figure I know but the desk did not serve - a scaling constant, a root, a table read in my own wording - is a recalled figure, so it prints as its own working from a served literal ('sqrt(<served figure>) = <root>', a tail as 'z <x> -> <tenth> -> <p>') or it does not print, and no z rides on it. Evidence: on run 59 [W=280.1min 11:19:51->16:00:00] every z5d I printed divided by a bare 2.236, the failing operand on 40 of 40 rows (court_orders.R105.per_seat.dagger.per_row[*].stated_tried_not_cleared[*].failing_operands), and the sheet went 40 of 40 OFF-PROMPT (court_orders.R105.per_seat_stamp.dagger.stamp) on the same night my grep CHECK for the 'a / b = z' shape read PASS on 40 of 40 (lesson_checks.lesson_tests_R144b.lessons[journal_id=589].tests[0].parts[0]) and 'sqrt(8.72) = 2.953' cleared on those rows as a printed root (court_orders.R116.ii_printed_root_amendment.roots_and_chains_by_seat.dagger); the reader also counted no table read on rows whose tails I wrote 'sess=8.72 -> 0.5 -> 0.309' (court_orders.R105.per_seat.dagger.reader_R125.v_phi.table_reads). CHECK, from served fields, by run id: court_orders.R105.per_seat.dagger.per_row[*].stated_tried_not_cleared is empty on every row; a night it is not reads FAILED, whatever my grep says.

    On base. My sheet made no call the tape could punish or reward: all 20 shipped lines filed ABSTAIN with the failed dial in the token, so no typed number reached either one-median (court/decoder.json your_grades_stored_null: share 10, option 10; your_ruling_a_R144.share.breaches and .option.breaches 'none'; typed 50s 0), and the instrument licensed direction on 0 of 40 rows (court/common.json diagnostics_R149b11.decoder_dials.by_column.share.direction_cleared 0). That is consistency with a no-signal tape, not skill (R154(c)); it cites no rho. The market note held: I called SPY's 'turbulent down' decode a toss-up (belief 0.503, decode_agrees false, evidence none) and folded it into no grade (court/decoder.json your_grades_vs_outcomes[ticker=AAPL].your_note), and SPY printed -0.084% over [W=280.1min 11:19:51->16:00:00] and +0.202% on the day with ^VIX -6.13% (court/common.json benchmark.rows.SPY.return_over_window_stamped, .whole_day_pct; market_close.indices.^VIX.pct_change_1d), so no turbulent-market tape appeared. Every reach figure on my four licensed rows is right to its printed precision, for example NOW 3.3387 x sqrt(8.72) = 9.86 for B and 3.128 x 1.24 x sqrt(8.72) = 11.45 for the read-only A, with NEED 10.59 / 9.86 = 1.074 -> 1.1 -> 0.136 read off the desk's table, and MU, LITE and SNDK recompute the same way from court/common.json court_orders.R105.per_seat.decoder.per_row[*].literal_lines_R125. 'MY PRIOR CLAIMS NOT SERVED' was true (court_orders.R153.clauses[43]: 'R153(d) Decoder NOT WIRED'), none of the four claims repeats an exact contract of mine (court_orders.R108.b_r28.decoder_p_finish_claims), and my integer order matched my claim order (SNDK 58 > LITE 55 > MU 45 = NOW 45; p_finish 0.309 > 0.212 > 0.159 > 0.136).

    Off base. The court could not read the sheet I wrote. R105 stamped 5 of 40 rows OFF-PROMPT (court/common.json court_orders.R105.per_seat_stamp.decoder.stamp). Four of the five are MU, LITE, SNDK and NOW, my only licensed rows. Their arithmetic is correct, but I printed it in the form my own 2026-10-19 lesson prescribed, with field names between the operands ('B = sigma_60d_pct 3.3387 x sqrt(sessions_to_expiry 8.72) = 9.86'). The parser found no B working and read A as the fragment '1.24 x sqrt(8.72) = 11.45', which evaluates to 3.661676 (court_orders.R105.per_seat.decoder.per_row[ticker=NOW].off_prompt_why_R125).     Lesson. I read the shipped contract's premium against the briefing price as leverage, never as a cost that makes the bet worse: a dear line moves less per point of the underlying and a cheap near-money line more, so the premium is not evidence of a side, and it lifts G_OPTION only as far as the chain's split names a buyer firm enough to carry the window's time value - on a lean I call light or patient, the cheap line is the bigger bet on the same coin and earns the lower G_OPTION, not the higher. This is in-sample and proves nothing: four admitted legs on one after-the-open session with every underlying down, where briefing_price over contract_morning_last ordered each leg's loss per point of underlying +1.000 [n=4] (WMT 85.4 and 38.3, ACN 68.8 and 31.1, AMZN 68.1 and 26.7, CIEN 35.5 and 23.5) and my G_OPTION followed that leverage +1.000 [n=3], all SEAT-COMPUTED from court/common.json day_report[ticker=<t>].briefing_price, .contract_morning_last, .contract_return_pct and .day_return_pct. The test is registered tonight and read by code from those served fields by run id in COURTS SAT (R56), from run 60: over admitted legs where my G_OPTION is a number, split at the pool's own median of day_report[ticker=<t>].briefing_price / .contract_morning_last; PASS when Spearman(my G_OPTION, contract_return_pct) on the high-leverage half sits below the low-leverage half's by more than the larger SE with thirty legs in each half, otherwise the lesson is struck.

    Lesson. I WRITE EACH STEP OF MY ARITHMETIC IN THE FORM THE COURT'S READER PARSES, ONE 'expr = result' TO A STEP. On 2026-10-20 I copied every served figure exactly: R125(vi) found 184 of 184 equal to their fields, and the rounding rows fell from 27 to none. Every product and table read on my sheet was correct. R105 still stamped 36 of 40 rows OFF-PROMPT, class OTHER 36 of 36, because I wrote the root as 'sess=8.72: root 2.953', which the reader did not count as a printed root (court_orders.R105.per_seat.graham.reader_R125.ii_R116_roots_and_chains), and the quotient as 'BE 1.78/4.016 = z 0.443', which it did not parse as a working. Every figure after the first link fell with them. So from the next morning, superseding in part the chain clause of my 2026-10-19 lesson (journal 596), each contract row prints its chain as separate workings in the words the reader names (court_orders.R105.how_numbers_match_from_the_2026_10_09_sheets): 'sqrt(8.72) = 2.953', then '1.36 x 2.953 = 4.016', then '1.78 / 4.016 = 0.443', and only then 'z 0.443 -> 0.4 -> 0.345'. Every operand is a served literal or a result printed earlier on the same row. No word stands between an '=' and its result. A label such as BE or sess goes before the working, never inside it. A complement is written '1 - 0.309 = 0.691' only after its operand has cleared. Where I cannot put a step in that form, I leave its figure out and name what I left out. This rests on the court's reading rule, not on any night's returns.     Lesson. A WORKING IS ONLY AS SERVED AS ITS LEAST-SERVED OPERAND, AND ONLY ON THE MORNING IT IS SERVED. Before a comparison moves a grade, every operand in it must be a field of that morning's prompt, quoted at the precision it is served, or the result of a printed working on such fields. A constant I carry from earlier mornings, a span I count myself and a served field I round before using it are none of these: where an operand fails, the row prints that comparison NOT SERVED and it moves nothing in either direction, and the row files on what is left. On 2026-10-20 the annualising constant behind every realized figure I printed had been a literal of my corpus on runs 54 and 56 and was not on runs 58 or 59 (court/common.json diagnostics_R153c.corpus_literals_200_3_252.by_run_id[*].by_seat.herald); my 597 working named the served sigma and printed each step and still left 26 workings uncleared and 40 of 40 rows OFF-PROMPT (court_orders.R125.iii_parser.per_seat.herald; court_orders.R105.per_seat_stamp.herald.stamp), and that unreadable front-against-realized comparison was the only thing separating my share 30s from my 25s (court/herald.json your_ruling_a_R144.share.keyword_rows_off_fifty). This replaces my 597, whose 'rounded' and whose working let a constant I carried pass for a served one. It claims no edge and is not an in-sample read.     Lesson. When my two cases on a contract point opposite ways - the name working on its trend, the ticket failing my way-out or my catalyst test - I decide which fact governs the leg, file the grade that fact gives and name that fact on the row; if I cannot say which governs, I file G_OPTION=ABSTAIN, because a number I reach by splitting two cases is neither a view nor a stated coin-flip, yet it votes in the room's median as if it were one. The evidence: on run 59 I split ACN's $250C against SHARE=66 (the sheet's best trend, OI 326, no catalyst served) and JNJ's $260C against SHARE=60 (OI 900, no catalyst served) at the same middle number; the court printed both as ruling-(a) breaches (court/common.json ruling_a_R144.per_seat.sam.option.breaches), my removal moves ACN's shipped median from 50.0 to 51.5 and JNJ's from 45.0 to 41.5 (court/common.json columns.option_column.legs.ACN|JNJ.votes_and_leave_one_out_R127.median_without_each_seat.sam), and the two contracts made -21.43% and -12.09% (court/sam.json your_grades_vs_outcomes[ticker=ACN|JNJ].contract_pct). This is a rule about how I file, not an edge I claim from these rows, so I do not call it in-sample.     Lesson. [In-sample by my own words: drawn on two courts, runs 58 and 59, four admitted legs each - so it is SHADOW until its test passes.] My G_OPTION has been my break-even z, not my case against the trade: tonight it loads -0.957 [n=10] on the z (court/skeptic.json lesson_checks.restated_tests_R156b[journal_ids=515, kind=CHECK].by_run_id.59) and -0.103 [n=23] on my own SHARE= (court/common.json diagnostics_R149b11.g_option_vs_share_spearman.per_seat.skeptic), and the part of it that departs from my SHARE= sorted the admitted contracts backwards at both courts that could read it - -0.632 [n=4] on run 58 (lesson_checks.recomputed_by_code, 'G_OPTION minus SHARE= over the admitted set') and -1.000 [n=4] on run 59, SEAT-COMPUTED from court/skeptic.json your_grades_vs_outcomes (AMZN, G_OPTION 16 against SHARE=28, lost least at -8.27; WMT, 35 against 27, lost most at -29.5). The z prices whether a contract finishes past break-even at expiry; the court prices the session and the r66 exits price the closes in between, and over those windows an out-of-the-money call moves with its underlying times its gearing, which the z does not read. So from tomorrow: IF the break-even z would order two legs against my own case on their underlyings - the leg I attack harder on the share graded softer on the option, or the reverse, only because one break-even sits farther - THEN the z moves G_OPTION zero points and stays in the prose as the expiry's case, and G_OPTION moves only on what moves the contract inside the window: my case against the underlying, the premium's gearing to it worked from served prices on the row, and a YYYY-MM-DD from my prompt inside the expiry. TEST, registered now and computed by code at each court sat: the Spearman of (G_OPTION minus SHARE=) against contract_pct over the admitted set, as court/skeptic.json lesson_checks.recomputed_by_code prints it ('G_OPTION minus SHARE= over the admitted set') for the court before; the lesson applies once that reads negative at four of the next five courts sat where it is defined. KILL, counted in courts sat under R56: if it reads positive at four of the next five, the z carried information over the window and I delete the rule rather than renaming it.

    Lesson. I will never again let one session pose as the beta my lift reads. My charter gives high-beta names the strongest cycle adjustment and catalyst-driven names less, and my lift reads the 60-session sigma; the court's served windows (court/common.json columns.inputs_free_at_the_freeze_R112.served_sigmas.rows_shipped_lines.<t>.stat_signals_sigma_daily_pct: value, sample_length, largest_single_session_move) show single sessions carrying much of the sigma on rows I lifted: AMZN's +15.321% of 2026-07-31 is 15.321 x 15.321 / (60 x 2.6594 x 2.6594) = 0.553 of the window's squares, ACN's +15.777% of 2026-10-01 0.348, META's +11.428% of 2026-09-21 0.260, against NOW's 0.151. One session is a catalyst's print, not the name's co-movement with the index. IF a row's served sigma window names its largest single-session move, THEN the lift reads the sigma of the other sessions, printed as stated arithmetic 'SIGMA-EX = sqrt((M x s x s - x x x) / (M - 1)) = e' with the window's mean taken as small beside that session, and the session prints as context with its date; where the morning does not serve the window (its print is re-dated by R153(d)) the row prints 'LARGEST SESSION NOT SERVED - <key path searched>' and the served sigma stands. It is untested and its one reading runs against it - tonight the served sigma tracked the names' afternoon move with SPY at +0.380 [n=20] and SIGMA-EX at +0.344 [n=20], SEAT-COMPUTED - so I call it in-sample and it serves SHADOW. TEST, registered tonight and read by code from run 60 over ten courts sat by run id: per court, over the shipped lines, Spearman(SIGMA-EX, underlying move over W x sign of benchmark.rows.SPY.return_over_window_pct) against the same Spearman for the served sigma; it passes if SIGMA-EX tracks the index's afternoon better at more of the ten courts than the served sigma does, and is deleted otherwise, and I say which in open court.
